title: Arrays [Easy - Medium - Hard]
tagline: the row of numbered boxes — master walking it before running

placementQuiz.explain: Index counts from 0 — index 3 = fourth box.

options: every remaining item shuffles one slot left
placementQuiz.explain: Contiguous memory: gap must close by shifting.

placementQuiz.explain: Dynamic row with size knowledge; array is fixed and forgetful.

blocks.md: **An array is a corridor of numbered lockers. Number on door = index; content inside = value. Door numbers start at 0 and never skip.**

items: Direct jump: `a[i]` opens locker i instantly — no walking needed
`vector` = same corridor that can grow a new wing at the end (`push_back`)
Insert/delete in MIDDLE? Every later locker's content must shuffle — expensive feeling to remember

blocks.label: walking the corridor
blocks.py:
a = [4, 9, 2, 7, 1]
print(a[0], a[-1])            # first & last (negative indexing!)
for x in a:                   # full walk
    print(x, end=' ')

v = [4, 9, 2]
v.append(7)                   # grow: {4,9,2,7}
print(len(v))                 # vector knows its length

items.q: Array of size n — valid indices run…
items.explain: Off-by-one guard: last legal index is n-1.

items.q: Why is inserting at FRONT the most painful spot?
options: ALL n items shift right to open door 0

blocks.label: reverse via two hands (two-pointer)
blocks.py:
l, r = 0, len(a) - 1
while l < r:
    a[l], a[r] = a[r], a[l]   # swap ends
    l += 1; r -= 1            # walk inward

blocks.label: remove duplicates from SORTED array
blocks.py:
write = 1
for i in range(1, n):
    if a[i] != a[i-1]:        # new value discovered
        a[write] = a[i]       # compact forward
        write += 1
# write = count of unique values

blocks.md: **Write-pointer idea = keep what's good, overwrite junk in place.** Reappears everywhere: move zeros, partitioning, dedupe. Learn once, reuse forever.

items.q: Reverse makes how many swaps for even n?
items.explain: Each swap settles TWO positions; pointers meet mid.

options: duplicates must be adjacent for single-pass detection
items.explain: Unsorted duplicates scatter; set-based route needed instead.

options: save a[0], shift all left, drop saved at end
items.explain: One temp + n−1 shifts; try k=general later.

blocks.label: 2D basics — rows of lockers
blocks.py:
g = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]
for row in g:                 # row-by-row walk
    print(*row)
# grid[r][c] reads: row then column

blocks.md: Grid problems usually ask: walk row-wise (nested loops), column sums (outer=c), or diagonals (r==c / r+c==n−1). Spot which LINE the question lives on before coding.

revisionCard: Index starts 0; last = n−1; a[i] jumps instantly
Middle insert/delete = shuffle pain — remember cost feeling
Write-pointer compacts in place: dedupe · move-zeros · partition family
Two-pointer from ends: reverse · palindrome · pair hunts
Sorted ⇒ duplicates adjacent ⇒ single-pass dedupe legal
Grid = rows of lockers; identify THE line (row/col/diag) question lives on

glossary.def: Rewrite inside same array, no second buffer.
Cursor marking next good-slot during compaction.
Two cursors coordinating walks (ends-inward or chase).
Circular shift of elements by k slots.
Grid memory order: whole row 0, then row 1…
